purpose: Four-processor remote kernel sessions, before implementation. This unit is Linux-hosted; the Mac cross-architecture client and the rest of S8 remain outstanding.

input_evidence.recipe: PAX tools/fetch-wolf, fetch-limine, build-kernel --src kernel/kmain_console.lu, mkuser, mkinitramfs and mkimage with limine-initramfs-quiet.conf. The console runs /bin/ask tty. mkuser's CC hook adds -save-temps=obj: otherwise a random temporary object FILE symbol changes ask's bytes. Two fresh output directories agree without byte normalization.

oracle: The existing binary pins: GDB 15.1 and QEMU 11.1.2, with version and SHA-256 checked before a judged row. Capture twice on separate boots under KVM and TCG. Old one-processor artifacts and goldens are unchanged.

predictions.claim: GDB lists four QEMU CPUs as four distinct debugger threads. Trunk sniff lists only one; the comparison is red before the fix.

After one BSP instruction at reset, CPU selection exposes that CPU's own registers and frame. Trunk cannot select CPUs 2 to 4. Switching back must not reuse another CPU's cache; an invalid thread number leaves the selection unchanged.

A breakpoint at the existing pax_ap_main secondary-CPU entry has a repeatable first secondary-CPU stop. The stop reply's thread, current-thread line, frame and registers agree. Trunk does not synchronize its session thread with the stop reply.
A single step after the AP stop advances the selected CPU through vCont;s:THREAD and refreshes its registers/frame, rather than the BSP's.
A reconnect re-enumerates all CPUs and selects the stop actually reported, dropping the previous connection's caches.
The explicit row CPU count reaches QEMU and is bound to its golden. An invalid count or mismatched count is refused, not silently run as one CPU.
Forcing BSP ownership after an AP stop fails remote-smp4-ap-break; preserving the old CPU's cache across selection fails remote-smp4-select. Both fail by comparison, never by timeout.

comparison: Keep CPU count, identity, selection, stop ownership and instruction progression asserted. Existing port/path/terminal normalization only. If a secondary CPU's stop or another CPU's incidental frame makes two oracle captures unstable, record it and settle the comparison before changing debugger code; do not mask it with a broad SMP normalization.
scope: QEMU vCPUs, all-stop, at one and four processors. No scheduled-task enumeration, PAX kernel changes, assignments, flags types, DAP changes, Mac remote implementation or performance claims. Rows already green on trunk are regression guards, not natural reds.
